# Facts That Change {#sec-facts}



Prices, plans, accounts and free allowances change from month to month, so this book keeps
them in one place: a file in its source, `book/facts.yml`, which this appendix prints in full.
The chapters quote it rather than typing a price or a plan, so when a fact changes, one edit
and a rebuild update every page that mentions it, and this list. Each fact carries the date it
was checked against the official page linked beside it. By the time you read this, some will
have changed: follow the link, and trust the page over the book.

## Agents, chats and models {.unnumbered}

| Fact | As the book states it | Checked | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| What Claude Code's account must be | Claude Code needs a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise or Console account | 2026-11-18 | [page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) |
| What Claude Code costs | Claude Code, for one, needs a paid plan or pay-per-use billing | 2026-11-18 | [page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) |
| What Codex's account must be | Codex a ChatGPT sign-in or an API key | 2026-11-18 | [page](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth) |
| What Antigravity's account must be | Antigravity a Google account | 2026-11-18 | [page](https://antigravity.google/docs/faq) |
| Antigravity's free tier | a personal Google account can use Antigravity on its free tier, with a quota refreshed weekly | 2026-11-18 | [1](https://antigravity.google/docs/plans), [2](https://antigravity.google/docs/faq) |
| Web chats with a free plan | Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini each have a free plan | 2026-11-12 | [1](https://claude.com/pricing), [2](https://chatgpt.com/pricing), [3](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/) |
| Models enough for this book's prompts | Claude's Sonnet on medium effort, or Haiku for small edits, or OpenAI's Sol on low | 2026-11-12 | [1](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview), [2](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) |
| Where the vendors suggest starting for hard work | Anthropic suggests starting with Opus 5.5 for most workloads, and OpenAI with GPT-6 Astra for complex reasoning and coding | 2026-11-12 | [1](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview), [2](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) |

: Facts the chapters quote, with the date each was checked. {#tbl-facts}


## Model prices {.unnumbered}

| Model | What the vendor says it is for | Input / output, \$ per million tokens |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | "high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks such as classification, extraction, and routing" | 0.10 / 0.50 |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | "the best combination of speed and intelligence" | 2 / 10 |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | "long-running agentic coding and knowledge work" | 4 / 20 |
| Claude Fable 5.2 | "demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work" | 8 / 40 |
| GPT-6 Luna | "focused, high-volume tasks" | 0.10 / 0.50 |
| GPT-6.1 Terra | "visual reasoning, precise computer use, and clear, natural writing" | 1 / 5 |
| GPT-6.1 Sol | "near-Astra performance for complex work at a lower cost" | 2 / 10 |
| GPT-6 Astra | "the most demanding work" | 10 / 50 |

: List prices of eight models, in dollars per million tokens of input and output, checked 2026-11-12. {#tbl-prices}

Haiku's price is for prompts up to 100,000 tokens; longer ones cost five times as much. Subscriptions count usage differently from API prices, and which models you can choose depends on your plan and the agent's version. Sources: Anthropic's [pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) and [models](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview) pages and OpenAI's [models](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) pages.


These are *API* prices: what a program pays per token when it calls the model directly
(@sec-choose). Read them as a snapshot of the spread between small and large models, not as
numbers to plan with.

from your repository.
